artifacts.summary: Five-phase plan to make the write-time task-reference gate resolve task-ref-ok markers region-aware over the reconstructed post-edit file, with a tree-wide marker-hygiene pass first, a depth-counting shared parser, the six dispatch-named test cases, documented semantics, and a final redeploy plus full gate verification.

memory_candidates.content: A text-marker exemption convention (task-ref-ok, version-ok) whose literal token is matched as a plain substring is self-tripping: any prose that DESCRIBES the convention is itself parsed as a marker. Three of five imbalanced files in this repo were caused by header comments containing the literal ':begin' token, not by real markers. Corollary for parser changes: switching such a marker parser from a boolean in_block toggle to a depth counter with a well-formedness verdict is a fail-closed TIGHTENING, not a refactor -- a boolean toggle silently tolerates unterminated begins and extra nested begins, so the tree almost certainly already contains files that parse to eof_depth > 0. Sequence the work as (1) a tree-wide hygiene pass that rebalances markers while the OLD parser is still live (semantically inert under a boolean toggle, hence independently verifiable), then (2) the parser change, then (3) a standing balance diagnostic so the condition cannot re-accumulate. A single awk depth-trace over git ls-files (count begin +1, end -1 clamped at 0, report eof_depth and first unclosed line) closes the 'which files might break' question in one pass before any code is written. Documentation about such a convention should name the markers without embedding the parseable substring.
